transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

That is probably a mechanical door-balance problem, not a latch or electrical fault. The springs/cables at the hinges normally counterbalance the door; if one breaks, slips off or the hinge wears, the door becomes heavy and drops open. Because it is built in, the furniture door can also affect the balance if its fixings have loosened or it has moved. 1. Switch the dishwasher off at the socket or isolator. Open the door slowly while supporting its weight. Check whether it feels unusually heavy or drops suddenly — that points to a failed hinge spring/cable.
2. Look along the edges of the fitted kitchen door panel for looseness, rubbing, or screws that have worked free. Do not remove panels or hinge covers. Any movement or misalignment may be the simpler cause.
3. Avoid letting it crash down repeatedly: support it when opening, as the extra strain can damage the remaining hinge parts or the furniture panel. If the panel is secure and the door is simply heavy and will not hold at any position, an engineer will normally need to inspect and replace the door hinge/balance spring or cable assembly. The exact arrangement varies, so it is not a sensible part to choose without the full model details and an inspection.
Tried it. The left side still has a bit of tension but the right side has none at all. I heard a twang last week when it went. Door closes and latches fine though.

This points to the right-hand door-balance assembly: most likely its cable or spring has snapped or come off, with the hinge/anchor a less common alternative. The twang followed by no tension on that side is very typical. The latch is not the cause, since the door still closes and latches normally. 1. Switch it off and isolate it. Support the door as you open it, as it can drop suddenly.
2. From the outside only, look around the lower right-hand hinge area for a loose cable, broken spring, or a fixing that has pulled away. Do not remove side panels or hinge covers. - A loose or broken cable/spring suggests the balance mechanism failure. - Nothing visible does not rule it out; the failed part is often behind the side panel. Avoid using the door unsupported. This is normally an engineer repair, as access to the spring/cable and hinge mechanism on an integrated dishwasher usually requires the appliance to be pulled out and dismantled. They should inspect both sides and replace the failed balance component(s), rather than fitting a latch.

I had a look under the plinth at the sides with a torch and can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side. I can't pull the machine out though, it's screwed to the worktop and the plinth is tight.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
The loose right-hand spring suggests the door-balance mechanism has failed on that side. That is why the door has no support and crashes down; it is not a latch fault. As the machine is fixed under the worktop and cannot be pulled out, this is best left to an appliance engineer. They will normally need to withdraw the integrated dishwasher, inspect the right-hand hinge, cable and spring anchor, and replace the failed balance component(s). Keep supporting the door when opening it and avoid letting it drop, as that can damage the remaining hinge parts or furniture door. Please send the full model number from the rating label, usually visible on the side edge of the open dishwasher door. That will identify the correct door-balance parts; do not rely on the Hotpoint brand alone.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The sticker on the door edge is partly peeled, all I can read is it starts with LTF. Is that enough, or do I just get an engineer in?

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
“LTF” is only a Hotpoint model-series prefix, so it is not enough to identify the exact replacement balance parts. It does, however, fit the sort of integrated dishwasher arrangement being discussed. Given the loose spring, no tension on the right, and the machine being fixed in place, I would get an appliance engineer in rather than trying to obtain a part from “LTF” alone. Ask them to inspect the right-hand hinge, cable and spring/anchor, and compare the left side; the failed balance component is the repair needed, not the door latch. If you can recover the rest of the model number it may help the engineer source parts before attending, but it does not need to delay booking the repair. Keep supporting the door whenever it is opened until it is fixed.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
